mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National civil registry, passport authority, or competent local government of the holder's country

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, and authorized signatories against the OFAC SDN List, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, European Union consolidated restrictive measures, and the French national asset-freeze list maintained by the Direction Générale du Trésor; mandatory PEP determination under CMF Article L.561-10 with enhanced due diligence and continuous monitoring for any PEP exposure; all results recorded in the pre-incorporation AML dossier.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) and INPI RNE search portal (data.inpi.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed SAS name must be lawful, non-misleading, and available; statutory documents are in French; a non-French name may be used but must be written in Roman characters on the public register, and where the source name is in non-Latin script a sworn French transliteration must be filed with the constitution file.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected as identical or confusingly similar to a registered name or as violating public order, the applicant may: (1) within 15 business days request a formal availability reprint from the INPI registry; (2) submit an administrative appeal letter directly to the RNE/INPI registrar; (3) if the rejection continues, file a judicial appeal before the Tribunal de commerce or the competent civil court within two months; and (4) alternatively file a new availability search and re-submit a modified corporate name through the Guichet unique.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A commercial domiciliation service and executive-office provider is accepted for a low-risk digital services SAS, provided the domiciliary agreement includes physical availability of a registered-seat office, mail reception, and handling of process service; a pure cloud/virtual address without any physical office is not sufficient as the sole registered seat.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; estimated at less than 5 percent annual probability for an unlicensed low-risk email-infrastructure SaaS company with clean document compliance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Title VII, Articles L.227-1 to L.227-30 (Société par Actions Simplifiée); general company provisions under Articles L.210-1 to L.210-12; registration obligations under Articles L.123-1 et seq. and R.123-1 et seq.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registry of the Commercial Court) within whose territorial jurisdiction the registered office is located; filings are made electronically through the Infogreffe national portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form M0 — Déclaration de création de société (CERFA No. 11677*06) together with the duly executed 'statuts' (articles of association) and supporting annexures.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for an SAS; the capital is freely fixed in the articles of association. Cash contributions must be paid up in accordance with the articles and deposited into a blocked escrow account at a French credit institution or the Caisse des Dépôts before registration; a capital deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt de fonds) is mandatory for the M0 filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: UNANIMOUS FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE SAS. WHEREAS the sole shareholder has reviewed the final draft articles of association, the first corporate resolution is adopted as follows: (1) the articles of association are approved in final form; (2) the share capital, fixed in Article 6, is subscribed in full and cash subscriptions are deposited in the blocked formation escrow account; (3) the registered office is established at 14 Rue de la République, 75003 Paris, France; (4) [Full Name] is appointed President with full powers to represent the Company; and (5) all officers and external counsel are authorized to publish legal notices, file the M0 registration form, and execute any regulatory formalities to complete incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the statutory constitution deed and declaration of conformity
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate counsel or, where notarization is chosen, the Notaire in the department of the registered office; notarization is mandatory only for contributions in kind of real property or certain other assets.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: a. Prepare the final draft of the statuts in accordance with the shareholder-approved model. b. Verify that the corporate name is available through the INPI infringement search and the RCS opposition database. c. Have each cash shareholder execute the statuts; if a notary is used, the notarial deed replaces the private deed. d. Sign the statutory 'déclaration de conformité' confirming that the statuts conform to applicable law. e. Preserve the signed originals securely as they must be lodged with the registration file.
required_dossiers: Shareholder passports or national identity cards
Draft bank capital certificate or notarial certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry or the notary queries a signature, missing annexure, or share allocation, cure by re-executing the relevant signature page and filing a corrective private deed or notarial act; adverse name objections may be cured by selecting a new distinctive sign and amending the statuts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of a blocked capital deposit account and issuance of the capital certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (CDC) acting as official depositary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: a. Open a non-trading account for the company 'en formation' at a French bank or CDC. b. Transfer the called cash share capital into the account and obtain the banker's 'attestation de dépôt de fonds' certifying the deposit amount. c. Instruct the banker that the funds are irrevocably blocked until registration. d. Have the bank release the funds to the company only after presentation of the K-bis extract or, if incorporation is refused, return the funds to the subscribers.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of shareholders and legal representatives
Bank KYC forms and source-of-funds declaration
List of subscribers and individual cash subscription amounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays the capital certificate due to compliance doubts, supply enhanced due diligence documentation (source of funds, tax identification, corporate biography). If the bank refuses the account, use the CDC deposit window or choose another French-licensed bank without modifying the statutory capital.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the legal constitution notice in an authorized legal gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A 'Journal d'annonces légales' (JAL) approved by the Prefecture for the department where the registered office is located.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: a. Prepare the constitution notice containing the corporate name, upon which the corporate form SAS, capital amount, registered office address, object, duration, and names of the President and statutory auditors if any. b. Submit the notice to the selected JAL and pay the publication fee. c. Verify the exact wording against the statuts before printing. d. Obtain the certificat de parution (publication certificate) issued by the JAL for attachment to the M0 file. The publication must take place within the time limits set by the Code de commerce.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney if filing counsel acts for the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL publishes a defective notice, publish a corrective rectificatif in the same journal and file the correction together with the original certificate; the registry will accept the consolidated publication if the first notice was validly placed within the legal deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the single registration dossier with the Commercial Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (in Alsace-Moselle, Greffe du Tribunal Judiciaire); filing is performed electronically through the Infogreffe portal as a single unique filing with the Formalités des Entreprises unit.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: a. Log into the Infogreffe online portal or use the government's formalités-entreprises service. b. Complete Form M0 (CERFA No. 11677*06) with the precise corporate data. c. Upload the notarized or private statuts, the capital deposit certificate, the JAL publication certificate, the declaration of conformity, the proof of registered-office occupancy (attestation de jouissance), identities of legal representatives, and any powers of attorney. d. Verify the automatic transmission of the dossier to the Greffe. e. Pay the compilable filing duties and taxes through the secure payment portal. f. Monitor the dossier status until the registry issues the K-bis extract.
required_dossiers: Attestation de dépôt de fonds (capital certificate)
Attestation de jouissance du local (occupancy consent)
Letters of appointment or notarial powers of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe flags the dossier with an 'observation', respond with the requested documents within the statutory 30-day cure period. If the application is rejected, amend the defective attachments and resubmit through Infogreffe without restarting the legal publication; in cases of unlawful refusal, seek an order from the commercial court president or file a new application with corrected formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of the K-bis extract and post-registration activation of tax, social, and data-protection registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Infogreffe for the K-bis; INSEE for SIREN/SIRET; Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) for VAT; URSSAF for employer social declarations; CNIL for data-processing registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: a. Upon successful registration, retrieve the official K-bis extract showing the RCS number and legal personality. b. Confirm automatic issuance of the SIREN and SIRET identifiers. c. Complete the 'début d'activité' declarations through the DGFiP online portal to obtain a French VAT number and the reimbursement threshold code. d. Register as an employer with URSSAF and establish the payroll account. e. File the required CNIL declaration for personal-data processing and appoint a data-protection officer if required by the GDPR. f. Open the definitive corporate bank account and transfer the formation escrow funds into the company's operating account.
required_dossiers: Proof of registered-office occupancy for tax records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the K-bis is delayed, request a certificate of delay from the Greffe and issue a formal reminder through Infogreffe; if SIREN/SIRET are not generated, contact INSEE with the dossier reference; for VAT delay, submit the DGFiP individual initiation request and provide the K-bis as proof; for payroll and CNIL errors, file corrective declarations on the respective portals.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — ISIC 6201 (Bulking Transactional Email API and Newsletter Hosting Platform) is a purely digital-data-service activity and does not constitute a classified industrial installation under the French Environmental Code (Code de l'environnement). The relevant digital-regulatory authorities are the Direction Générale des Entreprises (DGE) for service regulation and the CNIL for personal-data processing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating license or manufacturing permit is required. The service is carried out under ordinary commercial registration and is subject to horizontal EU digital regulations including the Digital Services Act (Regulation (EU) 2022/2065) and the ePrivacy Directive.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: DREAL — Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement, acting as the French environmental authority; for regional jurisdiction over Paris, the competent agency is the Direction Régionale et Interdépartementale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et des Transports (DRIEAT).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the proposed activity is administrative and digital in nature, with no land use, physical manufacturing, hazardous substance use, or mandatory listed facility threshold; therefore no full EIA report or environmental registration is triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater or VOC discharges are generated from the software/email hosting activity. Office premises must comply with municipal waste-sorting obligations and the WEEE Directive 2012/19/EU transposed in France for any discarded electronic equipment; cloud/data-center infrastructure operated by third parties remains independently responsible for emissions permits and environmental reporting. The company must maintain waste transfer documentation for office electronic waste.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Occupational clearance: the leased office must be fit for category ERP (Espace Recevant du Public) or ERT (Espace de Travail) occupancy with valid fire-safety certificates and compliance with French accessibility rules. Workplace arrangements must satisfy the Labor Code (Code du travail) requirements on lighting, ventilation, hygiene, and electrical safety. No civil-defense industrial clearance applies because the activity does not involve classified sites or dangerous substances.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — French tax administration, with main portal at impots.gouv.fr; corporate registration and SIREN issuance are channelled through the Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques (INSEE) via the Guichet Unique des formalités des entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must first register with the Guichet Unique to obtain a SIREN/SIRET if it creates a French permanent establishment or subsidiary. A French SAS is a separate legal entity and must file an incorporation dossier for automatic assignment of SIREN, APE/NAF code, and a VAT identification number. For direct cross-border VAT registration without a French establishment, the foreign taxable person must apply to the competent Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) using Form 3555-SD, indicating no French fixed establishment; VAT registration is generally granted within two to four weeks and the VAT ID is issued by the DGFiP. There is no statutory minimum capital requirement for a SAS and non-resident ownership is unrestricted, but the manager (président) or a tax representative may be required for non-EU persons.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A French SAS is automatically classified as a corporation subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) under Article 206 of the CGI. No general 'check-the-box' regime exists under French domestic law. Available elections include: (i) option for tax consolidation (intégration fiscale) under CGI Articles 223 A to 223 W for 95%-owned subgroups; (ii) option for the parental territoriality regime (régime mère-fille) and similar tax treatment; (iii) option for VAT grouping (assujetti unique) under Article 256 C III (permitted since 1 January 2023); and (iv) elections relevant to hybrid mismatch rules under Article 212 bis CGI transposing ATAD, including adjustments where a foreign entity is treated as transparent. French law also permits a small enterprise election for share-ownership plans but does not permit an SAS to pass through its income to shareholders other than in exceptional jointly owned vehicle cases, which are not available to this entity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA under Articles 256 to 256 ter of the Code Général des Impôts; aligns with EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a French-established taxable person, there is no general de minimis registration threshold: any economic activity carried out in France requires VAT registration. For non-established suppliers of digital and e-services to French consumers, the EU-wide EUR 10,000 annual distance-sales threshold applies; above this, OSS (One-Stop Shop) registration is available. For purely French domestic distance sales of goods by EU taxable persons, the threshold is EUR 35,000. Since this entity is a French SAS, it is required to hold a French VAT number irrespective of turnover, and should charge French VAT on B2C supplies of email infrastructure services in France.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is progressively mandating electronic invoicing for domestic B2B transactions: mandatory e-invoicing and structured e-reporting begins 1 September 2026 for large enterprises and 1 September 2027 for SMEs. Invoicing must be transmitted through a certified Partner Dematerialization Platform (PDP) or the public Portal Public de Facturation (PPF); no continuous transaction-control or real-time fiscal clearance (visa or digital stamping) is currently enforced for ordinary VAT invoices. For export/zero-rated transactions, the classical paper/electronic invoice requirements of Article 289 CGI still apply, and e-reporting of B2B international transactions is required once the measure is in force.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods, zero-rating applies under Article 262 CGI when the goods physically leave the European Union and are evidenced by a customs export declaration (DAO/ENS). For services, including email infrastructure and newsletter hosting, French VAT is not charged on supplies of services to a customer established outside the European Union when the services are effectively used and enjoyed outside the EU (Article 259 A and 259 C CGI). For EU B2B supplies, the place of supply is the customer's establishment and VAT is reverse-charged in the customer's Member State. A French SAS may also zero-rate export-related services directly linked to exported goods, but ordinary SaaS services are generally outside the scope of French VAT for non-French customers rather than 'zero-rated'.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration en Douane / DAU-ENS with MRN)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill (or CMR for road transport)
Proof of settlement (Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement evidencing FX repatriation)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGFiP rigorously audits export zero-rating claims and may re-invoice VAT plus interest if the documentary evidence is incomplete or false. Fraudulent or abusive zero-rating exposed to penalties under Articles 1728 and 1729 CGI: late-payment interest (0.20% per month) and an additional penalty of 40% for bad faith or 80% for deliberate tax evasion or artificial arrangements; criminal sanctions under Article 1741 CGI may include a fine of up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment of up to five years, with publicity of the conviction. A retrospective clawback period of ten years applies for hidden or fictitious transactions (Article L. 169, Livre des procédures fiscales).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (central bank of France; General Directorate of Operations and Statistics), in concurrence with the Direction Generale du Tresor on capital-movement and investment screening, and the ACPR (Autorite de Controle Prudentiel et de Resolution) for banking and prudential supervision; monetary policy authority remains with the European Central Bank within the euro area.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France applies full euro convertibility under Article 63 TFEU. Current-account payments, commercial settlements, and profitremittance transactions are unrestricted and require no Bank of France exchange-control permit. Capital-account transactions, including euro share-capital injections, shareholder loans, and treasury transfers, are generally free for a non-sensitive French SAS active in email/newsletter infrastructure software. A cross-border direct investment in France may, however, require prior authorization under Decree 2019-1590 if it falls within a strategic sector; ISIC 6201 bulk transactional email and newsletter hosting is not a designated sensitive sector. Profit remittance hurdles are tax-oriented, not exchange-control-oriented: a French distributing SAS must prove the distributor decision, the existence of distributable profits under Article L232-11 of the Commercial Code, the beneficial ownership of the shareholder, and the applicable withholding-tax or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief. No central-bank permission is required for dividend transfers to non-residents.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no statutory surrender requirement, no mandatory repatriation timeline, and no forced conversion ratio for export proceeds or cross-border digital-service receivables. The SAS may retain export receivables in foreign currency or convert them at market rates on a voluntary basis. French credit institutions are, however, obligated under the Banque de France balance-of-payments reporting framework to classify and transmit cross-border payment information, including a BOP purpose code and the economic nature of the underlying transaction, usually when an individual operation reaches or exceeds the EUR 50,000 regulatory statistical-reporting threshold. The company should retain customer contracts, commercial invoices, SWIFT confirmations, and evidence of service delivery so that the bank can correctly code the flows and defend any audit inquiry.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account or Operational Account
Operational Account and Short-Term Treasury Sweep

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: High for auxiliary collection/disbursement rails, Low-Medium for core treasury concentration. An offshore digital EMI that is outside the EEA cannot lawfully passport payment or e-money services into France; it must be licensed or passported in France/EEA under PSD2 and the French Monetary and Financial Code. Regulated EEA EMIs can be used for customer pay-ins such as Stripe Billing settlement, virtual-account segmentation, and fast international payouts. Legal constraints: EMI balances are safeguarded funds, not bank deposits; they are not covered by the French deposit-guarantee fund, and the EMI cannot provide credit, term deposits, or structured treasury products. For a low-risk SaaS treasury, the prudent board policy is to cap idle balances at an EMI at approximately two times monthly operating expenses and to wire residual liquidity to a Banque de France-supervised credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no absolute statutory requirement that all directors appear physically at a French bank branch; ACPR-compliant remote onboarding is permitted when the bank performs verified digital identity checks and eIDAS-qualified electronic signatures. In practice, an EU-resident French or foreign director with a compliant biometric passport and clean KYC can often complete opening via video verification and a remote e-signature workflow. Non-EU directors without biometric EEA documentation, or corporate structures with complex offshore ownership, will normally be required to attend an in-person interview at a French branch or to work with a designated French legal representative/consulate notarization route. The target SAS should expect either a single physical appointment for its President or a hybrid remote process using a qualified trust-service provider and apostilled corporate documents, depending on the selected bank's risk appetite.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated SAS with non-resident ultimate beneficial owners and no domestic French banking relationship.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled constitutional documents of the SAS; current Kbis/extract from the Registre du Commerce et des Societes; registered beneficial-ownership declaration; complete share register; board/shareholder resolutions approving account opening and transaction authorization; valid passports plus residence certificates of all Directors and UBOs; tax residence certificates of all foreign UBOs; signed confirmation of source of funds/wealth; corporate chart with all intermediate entities; and a short legal opinion confirming the non-resident ownership structure is valid under French law and foreign investment rules.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Alleged mismatch between stated equity capital and projected cross-border SaaS transaction volumes, creating potential money-laundering or fraud-risk concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Financial business plan and three-year cash-flow forecast; customer pipeline and signed software-as-a-service contracts; proof of revenue model and unit economics; merchant acquiring or Stripe Billing account history where available; invoice templates; terms of service and data-protection documentation; existing suppliers' agreements for email-sending infrastructure; explanation of future shareholder-loan funding with signed loan agreements or compte courant d'associe terms; payroll and operational expenditure budget demonstrating the capital will be deployed in France/EU.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-card-volume subscription business with low average ticket values and potential aggregator risk through Stripe Billing/card payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed payment-processing flow showing merchant-of-record status; Stripe or payment-processor due-diligence package; PCI DSS compliance attestation; fraud-prevention and chargeback-management procedure; refund policy; subscriber verification and anti-abuse controls; acceptable-use policy prohibiting spam and illegal newsletter content; records of complaint handling; monthly reconciliation reports; and an external cybersecurity/AML program description demonstrating robust control.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Exposure of a newsletter-infrastructure platform to subscribers or counterparties located in sanctioned, embargoed, or high-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written global sanctions policy aligned with OFAC, EU, French, and UN sanctions lists; IP geoblocking and geo-fencing measures; subscriber onboarding terms requiring conformity with embargoes; denied-party and politically-exposed-persons screening procedures for enterprise customers; evidence of no transactions with listed entities; data-residency controls; sales and marketing restrictions for prohibited territories; and a named compliance officer accountable for sanctions screening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear economic substance and French operational nexus for a digital services holding/SAS, particularly where director or account signatory is non-resident.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: French registered office lease or domiciliation agreement; actual local management and board decision records; employment/management contract of the President; French tax and social-security filings; operating bank account evidence; recurring French/EU supplier invoices; office IT infrastructure and local equipment inventory; French VAT registration certificate for digital services; and reporting file demonstrating effective management is situated in France rather than in a mailbox or tax-planning structure.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound euro capital subscriptions must clear via SEPA or SWIFT direct to the SAS IBAN, but for a completed share-capital increase the funds should first be credited to a temporarily blocked bank account held in the name of the SAS or deposited with a French approved financial institution until the legal formalities are completed. The SWIFT MT103 should identify the ordering shareholder, the SAS beneficiary, and in Field 70 a clear legal reference such as /APPT/ Apport en capital, under a French BOP/NC-ECO purpose code identifying equity shares, not ordinary services. The bank will require an authenticated corporate resolution of the SAS approving the capital increase, supporting documentation of the contribution, inbound source-of-funds evidence, UBO confirmation for the shareholder, and any necessary Form 5000/5001 if treaty relief is claimed. For future director or shareholder liquidity injections, the routing should use a separate loan agreement and label the payment as Avance/Compte courant d'associe with arm's length interest terms to prevent recharacterization by the French tax administration. No French exchange-convertibility authorization is needed for a non-sensitive SaaS investment.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements and treasury outflows, use SEPA Credit Transfer for EEA suppliers, SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for time-critical European disbursements, and SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfer for non-EEA suppliers or multi-currency operational payments. Each instruction must include the original invoice number and a precise remittance narrative. A documentary commercial letter of credit is not market standard for pure SaaS or email-infrastructure services; if the company later imports hardware, servers, or network equipment, an irrevocable documentary credit under UCP600 may be opened at a French confirming bank via SWIFT MT700, payable against transport documents and a clean set of invoices. Outbound dividends and director fees should be transmitted by SEPA/SWIFT only after formal corporate decisions and, where applicable, tax withholding or treaty-relief documentation has been presented to the paying French bank. FX payments are generally unrestricted, but the bank must reconcile each disbursement with valid documentation and, when required, the relevant Banque de France balance-of-payments declaration.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX spot transactions on liquid EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF, and EUR/JPY markets, settled within standard T+2 clearing timelines
Plain-vanilla FX outright forwards, typically 1-12 months, with a confirmed underlying commercial exposure
FX swaps (swap de change), including tom/next swaps, to manage temporary euro liquidity and beneficiary currency positions
Non-deliverable forwards on restricted or non-deliverable currencies, only where settlement risk exists and the instrument is used to hedge, not speculate
Cross-currency swaps for structural balance-sheet matching when non-euro cash flows or financing liabilities exist, subject to EMIR confirmation and clearing thresholds
European-style FX options or zero-premium collar structures, permissible only under a board-approved treasury policy and with a regulated investment-services provider

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholder approval of financial statements and, where the SAS is not eligible for the small-company exemption, approval of the management report (rapport de gestion)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal governance record only; minutes entered in the statutory register of shareholders' decisions (no external filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the fiscal year-end under Code de commerce Article L232-1; a calendar-year SAS must approve by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Financial statements cannot be legally deposited; court may order the meeting on shareholder petition; failure to communicate accounts to shareholders exposes directors to a EUR 4,500 corporate fine (Code de commerce Article L232-23)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts (balance sheet, income statement, notes and, when audited, the statutory auditor's report) with the commercial registry (depot des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de commerce, filed electronically through the INPI Guichet Unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of shareholder approval and in all cases no later than seven months after fiscal year-end (calendar-year SAS: by 31 July)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Per-document fine up to EUR 4,500 (Code de commerce Article L232-23); commercial court injunction with per-day penalty (astreinte) on application of the public prosecutor; repeated non-filings expose the entity to administrative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return Form 2065 and the full tax package (liasse fiscale 2065-SD) covering corporate income tax and the transfer-pricing annexes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Generale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), mandatory electronic filing on impots.gouv.fr
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Second working day following 1 May for fiscal years closed on 31 December (5 May 2025 and 2026); for non-calendar year-ends, within 90 days of the close
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 10% of the assessed tax, rising to 40% after formal notice (80% for fraudulent intent), plus monthly late-payment interest of 0.20%; DGFiP may issue a unilateral tax assessment and reassess the taxable base

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business contribution (Cotisation Fonciere des Entreprises - CFE) payment against the tax bill issued by the local tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP local tax collection office (poste comptable) on behalf of the communes and EPCI where registered activity exists on 1 January
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payment by 15 December of each year for the current-year CFE; new establishments file Form 1447-C within 90 days of commencement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic 10% late-payment increase plus 0.20% monthly interest (CGI Articles 1730 and 1731); enforced recovery through a state warrant (avis de mise en recouvrement) with no prior demand

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Transfer-pricing documentation (master file and local file) retained and available to tax inspectors at the income tax return deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP tax audit service; not filed but must be produced within 30 days of an audit request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same due date as Form 2065; obligation assessed annually on entities with annual turnover or gross assets of at least EUR 400 million or heading a group with consolidated turnover of at least EUR 400 million
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to produce documentation after formal notice triggers an EUR 15,000 fine (CGI Article L13AA); where transfer pricing is challenged, penalties of 5% of the reassessed profits with a EUR 10,000 minimum (CGI Article L13AB)

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) must be appointed when the SAS exceeds two of three thresholds at fiscal year-end: balance sheet total above EUR 6,000,000; net turnover excluding VAT above EUR 12,000,000; or average workforce above 50 employees. Below those thresholds the audit is voluntary, although shareholders holding at least 10% of the capital may petition the court to appoint an auditor
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French statutory accounts under French GAAP (PCG - Autorite des Normes Comptables Regulation 2014-03, as amended); IFRS as adopted by the EU applies only to consolidated financial statements, never to the individual statutory accounts of an SAS

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France applies a declaration-upon-change regime rather than an annual UBO confirmation: the SAS must declare any modification of its effective beneficiaries (beneficiaires effectifs) to the commercial registry via the Guichet Unique within 30 days of the change. Each annual accounts deposit package confirms the current shareholding structure; SAS share transfers are mandatorily recorded in the share-movement register and, when the transfer alters control or UBO composition, trigger the 30-day updating declaration
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of shareholders' decisions (registre des decisions des associes)
Register of share movements and transfers (registre des mouvements de titres)
Minute book and authenticated minutes of collective decisions (proces-verbaux)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - 1,500 per year for a professional domiciliation service (domiciliation commerciale), standard range for Paris and major French cities
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 - 12,000 per year for a certified statutory audit (commissaire aux comptes) of a small or medium SAS

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard rate (Article 219 CGI) from 1 January 2022; reduced rate of 15% applies to the first EUR 38,120 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs (turnover below EUR 10 million and capital held at least 75% by individuals).
